_comment: Project checks, added to the baseline checks built into tools/hooks/hooks.mjs (BASE_REQUIREMENTS). An entry with a baseline tag overrides it; turning a baseline check off needs disabled: [{tag, reason}]. Each entry: when (all true) -> require (all must hold), else block with message. Conditions: promptMatches, promptNotMatches, answerMatches, answerNotMatches, minToolCalls, workTurn, filesChanged, allFilesChanged, toolRan, toolUsed, resultMatches, fileRead, playbookRouted, playbookUsed, skillUsed, toolPassed {cmd, pass, selfRun}, runEach {files, cmd}. Every tag needs a row in docs/checks/rule-enforcement.md and a test in tools/hooks/selfcheck.mjs.

requirements.message: Save the plan to docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md (plan skill) and link it in the answer, then ask the user to review it before work starts (with "autonomy": "auto", carry it out and record your choices instead).
Debug skill: state the root cause in the answer ("Root cause: <what and why>") with the evidence that shows it, found before the fix.

Debug skill: code changed for the fix, but no test did. Add a test that fails without the fix and passes with it, and run the suite. If the project has no test framework, write "N/A(debug-test-added): no test framework" and say how the fix was checked instead.
Parallel-agents skill: run the full checks on the combined result after the last change, and say in the answer what they showed, part by part.

Answers from research cite their sources: end each fact with a numbered citation [1], [2], and end the answer with "Sources:" and one line per number, "[n] <link or project file>" (a markdown link [title](link) works too), each a source read this turn. Or say plainly that nothing is recorded in the project.
Research skill: the answer says it is verified, so its ledger must pass: node skills/research/scripts/claims.mjs check .cache/research/<slug>.md, and fix every ERROR.
Skill-finder skill: report the search in the answer: "Existing skills checked: <where> - <result>".

Skill-finder skill: a third-party skill was brought in and changed. Check the wording is ours: node tools/skills.mjs compare skills/<skill> <the untouched copy> must print "0 shared run(s)". Rewrite every shared run it lists.
Plan skill: run node skills/plan/scripts/plan-tasks.mjs check <plan> and fix each warning (or give its reason) before handing the plan over.
Security-review skill: end with the report table: every area PASS, FAIL or N/A with its evidence, and where each open FAIL went.
Security-review skill: log the review in the Reviews table of docs/security.md (date, scope, result, open FAILs and where they went).

requirements.message: This turn wrote security-sensitive code (sign-in, passwords, tokens, secrets, permissions, sessions, cookies, CORS, uploads, endpoints, shell or eval, query building, deserializing, crypto, payments or personal data). Follow the security-review skill for what changed (its report table and the log line in docs/security.md), even though nobody asked. If the match is not security work, waive it with N/A(security-code): <the specific reason, e.g. "the word is a CSS class name">.

This turn changed secrets, the build pipeline or deployment settings (.env, CI workflows, Docker, hosting, infrastructure). Follow the security-review skill for those areas (Secrets, Deployment, Build pipeline, Access to infrastructure), or waive it with N/A(security-config): <the specific reason>.

requirements.message: Something was published or deployed this turn. Hard rule 15: the security-review skill runs before anything is shared, published or released. Follow it now, log it in docs/security.md, and tell the user what it found.

A test or build failed this turn and code was changed after it: that is a fix, so the debug skill applies. Say what was wrong and why ("Root cause: <what and why>", with the evidence), found before the fix. A test written first to fail on purpose: "Root cause: the feature did not exist yet".

Several sub-agents worked this turn: their results are only done once checked together (parallel-agents skill). Run the full checks on the combined result after the last change and say what they showed, part by part.
